name: Wynn Bullock
notes: Appears at plates #2 and #6 of the Prologue in the MoMA Master Checklist. Nationality 'American' per checklist. The prints are widely identified in secondary sources as 'Let There Be Light' (1954) and 'Child in Forest' (1951), but the checklist itself does not title or date them (see notes on photo-0002 and photo-0005).

name: Nat Farbman
notes: Plate #4 (Prologue, Belgian Congo). LIFE staff photographer, full name N. R. Farbman. Checklist nationality: American. Dates 1907–1988 filled from LIFE's own photographer-archive page (life.com/photographer/n-r-farbman, fetched 2026-04-24). Husband-and-wife photography team with Pat English from 1940 per LIFE's own archive; LIFE's page confirms Farbman's 'work on tribes in Botswana was included' in *The Family of Man* (verbatim quote), without specifying the year of the series or the number of plates. Note: current photo_count=1 reflects MoMA Master Checklist plate #4 only; if additional Farbman plates exist in the 503-image exhibition (the catalog is 192/503 as of this PR), photo_count should be revised during a future catalog-builder batch.

name: Harry Callahan
notes: Plate #9 (Prologue). Nationality 'American' per checklist. Born Detroit, died Atlanta. Taught at the Institute of Design (Chicago, 1946–61) and RISD (1961–77); MoMA holdings substantial.

name: Pat English
notes: Plate #10 (Prologue, England). Also documented as half of the Nat Farbman / Pat English husband-and-wife LIFE photography team per LIFE's own archive page for N. R. Farbman (fetched 2026-04-24). Checklist nationality: American. Gender left blank per plan.md §18 Q16 (self-identification or reputable-source documentation required; LIFE's archive description of her as 'former fashion model and photographer ... his wife' is third-party and does not itself satisfy the self-identification test). Birth/death years NOT sourced to any fetched reference this round (issue #13); remain blank pending a Tier-1/2 biographical source — LIFE's archive confirms her existence and role but does not publish her dates.

Harris 1913–1978') held at the American Geographical Society Library, UW-Milwaukee — identified via the Wikipedia article as Reference 1 per CREDIBILITY.md's pointer-only rule. name: Dmitri Kessel
notes: Plate #12 (Lovers, China). LIFE magazine. Checklist nationality 'American'. Born near Kyiv in the Russian Empire (present-day Ukraine); emigrated to the US in 1923 and naturalized. Scholarly sources variously describe him as 'Ukrainian-American' or 'American, born Ukraine'; checklist form preserved.

name: Ralph Morse
notes: Plate #13 (Lovers, England). LIFE magazine. Checklist nationality: American. Known for WWII combat, the Mercury Seven astronaut coverage, and early scientific-reportage photography.

name: Robert Doisneau
notes: Three plates in Section 2 Lovers (#14, #16, #20). Credited in the checklist via Rapho Guillumette agency. Checklist nationality: French. Born Gentilly, died Montrouge. The famously titled 'Le Baiser de l'Hôtel de Ville' (1950) is not confirmed as any of these three plates at the plate level — see notes on photo-0011.

name: Laurence Le Guay
notes: Plate #15 (Lovers, New Guinea). Checklist prints the surname as 'LeGuay' (one word); Australian publications print it 'Le Guay' (two words). We use 'Laurence Le Guay' as the canonical name with 'LeGuay' as a spelling variant. Checklist nationality: Australian. Birth year recorded as 1917 per the SMH obituary (src-leguay-1990-obit); Wikipedia lists 1916 but without a citation this repo can verify — flagged for reconciliation against the primary SMH obit or an AGNSW/State Library of NSW archival reference when access becomes available.

name: Lou Bernstein
notes: Plate #17 (Lovers, USA). Brooklyn street and Coney Island photographer; Photo-League-adjacent. Checklist nationality: American. Dates per Tier-3 obituary reference — see source file's verification flag.

name: Roy DeCarava
notes: Plate #18 (Lovers, USA). Checklist prints 'Roy De Carava' (two words); canonical form is 'DeCarava' (one word) per the photographer's own estate and his 1996 MoMA retrospective catalog. We use 'Roy DeCarava'. First African-American photographer to receive a Guggenheim Fellowship (1952); 1955 book *The Sweet Flypaper of Life* with Langston Hughes. Checklist nationality: American.

name: Gotthard Schuh
notes: Plate #19 (Lovers, Italy). Checklist nationality: Swiss. Born Berlin-Schöneberg (German-born) but raised in Switzerland and a lifelong Swiss citizen — checklist form preserved. Picture editor at Zürcher Illustrierte in the 1930s; Bali/Java reportage (1938–39). Fotostiftung Schweiz, Winterthur, holds the estate archive.

name: David Linton
notes: Plate #21 (Lovers, USA). Checklist nationality: American. Biographical dates NOT sourced. Issue #13 search outcome: moma.org/artists/66480-david-linton was attempted and returned 403 (2026-04-24); the MoMA page content was never read, so its contents (exhibition years, biographical summary) are unverified. No other fetched source this round supplied birth/death years. Name disambiguation flag preserved: multiple people named 'David Linton' exist (incl. a British-American geographer and a contemporary UK commercial photographer) — do not assign dates without a confirmed single-person identification via a successful MoMA fetch or a Tier-1 obituary.

name: Wayne Miller
notes: Six plates in the first 47 checklist numbers (#22, #29, #42, #43, #44, #47). Steichen's curatorial assistant on *The Family of Man*; later president of Magnum Photos (1962–66). Born Chicago, died Orinda, CA. Checklist nationality: American.

name: Louis Faurer
notes: Two plates in Lovers (#23, #25). Born Philadelphia, died New York City. Checklist nationality: American. New York School photographer; commercial / fashion work for Junior Bazaar, Harper's Bazaar, Vogue.

name: Ernst Haas
notes: Plate #24 (Lovers, scene in USA; photographer nationality Austrian per checklist). Magnum member from 1949; pioneer of color reportage. Born Vienna, died New York City.

name: Robert Capa
notes: Five plates in the catalog (count verified by grep this session, 2026-05-02): photo-0023 (Marriage, Czechoslovakia), photo-0118 (Land, USSR), photo-0131 (Land, USSR), photo-0246 (Food, USSR), photo-0274 (Ring Around the Rosy, Israel). Checklist nationality: 'American' (per US naturalization); scholarly convention used by ICP, Magnum, and the Richard Whelan biography is 'Hungarian-American' — born Endre Ernő Friedmann in Budapest, 22 Oct 1913; killed by a land mine on 25 May 1954 near Thai-Binh, Indochina, on *LIFE* assignment (per src-nyt-1954-capa-obit, in repo). Magnum Photos co-founder (1947) with Henri Cartier-Bresson, William Vandivert, David Seymour, and George Rodger; Magnum president 1952–1954. His brother Cornell Capa would later found the International Fund for Concerned Photography in his memory in 1966 (per src-icp-1966-concerned-photography-fund-institutional, in repo). Plate count corrected from 3 to 5 in this batch (PR #111); the prior 3 was a stale seed-batch figure.

name: Frank Horvat
notes: Plate #27 (Marriage, India). Checklist nationality: 'Italian' (per Horvat's 1928 birthplace in Abbazia, then within the Kingdom of Italy — today Opatija, Croatia). Scholarly sources describe him variously as Italian, Croatian (per post-1947 sovereignty), or French (per long residence). Black Star agency. Died Boulogne-Billancourt, France.

name: Hans Malmberg
notes: Plate #28 (Marriage, Sweden). Checklist nationality: Swedish. News photographer for *Se* and *Vecko-Journalen* in 1950s–60s Stockholm. Precise day/month dates not verified in this seed entry — Tier-1 Swedish archival sources preferred for future updates.

name: Werner Bischof
notes: Plate #30 (Marriage, Japan). Checklist nationality: Swiss. Born Zurich, 26 Apr 1916; died 16 May 1954 in the Peruvian Andes on *LIFE* assignment — nine days before his Magnum co-member Robert Capa. His plate was contributed to *The Family of Man* posthumously.

name: Brassaï
notes: Six plates in the catalog (count verified by grep this session): photo-0123 (Land, France), photo-0203 (Adult Play, France), photo-0250 (Food, France), and three others. Born Gyula Halász, 9 September 1899 in Brassó, Transylvania, Kingdom of Hungary, Austria-Hungary (now Brașov, Romania) per src-wikipedia-brassai-pointer (in repo). Died 8 July 1984 on the French Riviera (Wikipedia infobox names Beaulieu-sur-Mer; the body Death section says 'his home on the French Riviera near Nice') and was buried at Montparnasse Cemetery in Paris. Adopted his pseudonym from his birthplace. Naturalized French citizen in 1949. Best known for the 1933 publication *Paris de nuit*. Steichen also curated a separate MoMA exhibition of Brassaï's work in 1956 — the year after FoM.

name: David Seymour
notes: Four plates in the catalog: photo-0064 (Children A, Austria), photo-0276 (Ring Around the Rosy, Italy), photo-0304 (Relationships, Germany), photo-0320 (Learning, Italy). Born Dawid Szymin (also rendered Szymin), 20 November 1911 in Warsaw, Congress Poland. Died 10 November 1956 in El Qantara, Egypt — killed by machine-gun fire during the Suez Crisis. Naturalized U.S. citizen (1942). Known professionally as 'Chim'. Magnum Photos co-founder (1947) with Robert Capa, Henri Cartier-Bresson, William Vandivert, and George Rodger; became Magnum president after Capa's May 1954 death and held the post until his own November 1956 death. Renowned for Spanish Civil War photography and his 'Children of War' UNICEF project documenting post-WWII refugee children — thematically aligned with FoM's humanist register. All four Seymour plates carry the Magnum + UNESCO commissioner combination per the MoMA Master Checklist.

name: Elliott Erwitt
notes: Four plates in the catalog: photo-0034 (Pregnancy, USA), photo-0047 (Births, USA), photo-0178 (Work B, USA), photo-0359 (Religious Expression, USA). Born Elio Romano Erwitz, 26 July 1928 in Paris, France, to Jewish-Russian immigrant parents. Died 29 November 2023 in New York City. Family relocated to Italy, then emigrated to the United States in 1939. Magnum Photos member since 1953 (invited by founder Robert Capa); served U.S. Army 1951–1953. Known for black-and-white candid photographs of ironic and absurd situations. Cross-reference src-magnum-photographer-bios in repo (mentions Erwitt #37/#50 within multi-photographer Magnum bios; NOT re-fetched for Erwitt-specific verification this round). All four Erwitt plates set in the USA per the MoMA Master Checklist.

name: W. Eugene Smith
notes: Four plates in the catalog: photo-0099 (Children B, USA), photo-0333 (Learning, USA), photo-0367 (Aloneness and Compassion, USA), photo-0488 (Childhood Magic, USA — *A Walk to Paradise Garden*, 1946 — THE CLOSING IMAGE of the entire 503-plate exhibition per src-moma-archives-highlights-1955, in repo). Born 30 December 1918 in Wichita, Kansas; died 15 October 1978 in Tucson, Arizona (per src-wikipedia-w-eugene-smith-pointer, in repo). Wikipedia describes him verbatim as 'perhaps the single most important American photographer in the development of the editorial photo essay'. *A Walk to Paradise Garden* (1946) shows his two children walking hand in hand towards a clearing in woods; Steichen selected it as the closing image of FoM, anchoring the exhibition's redemptive 'return to children / new life' arc per the institutional MoMA-archives summary.
